newsitem.title: USA: US avg jobless period, long-term unemployment fall.
newsitem.headline: US avg jobless period, long-term unemployment fall.

text.p: The average length of unemployment and the total number of Americans unemployed for long periods of time both fell in March, the U.S. Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday.

The March employment report released Friday showed that the average duration of unemployment fell to 15.3 weeks in March, the lowest it has been since it hit 14.8 weeks in November 1991, said Philip Rones assistant BLS commissioner.
"It has come down fairly slowly," after moving as high as 19.4 weeks in October 1994 in the aftermath of the 1990-1991 recession, Rones said at a briefing on the March data.
The number of Americans who have been unemployed for 27 weeks or more has declined in recent months after being stuck at the same high level for roughly two years, Rones added.
The Labor Department's gauge of long-term unemployment -- 27 weeks or more -- had stayed "stubbornly high" at about 1.3 million over a two-year period, Rones said.
"For the first time it looks like it's come down," Rones said of the recent trend. It stood at 1.063 million in March, 1.138 million in February and 1.212 million in January.

Rones said the data showing the number of people unemployed for various periods of time provide a better gauge than the average duration of unemployment, which fails to reflect how many people are affected.
"Looking at the pieces gives you a better picture," Rones told Reuters. "This allows you to see where the action is."
